import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---
# Handle missing values in Income
df.dropna(subset=['Income'], inplace=True)

# Create new insightful features
# Total spending on different product categories
mnt_cols = [col for col in df.columns if 'Mnt' in col]
df['Total_Spending'] = df[mnt_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Total number of children in the household
df['Children'] = df['Kidhome'] + df['Teenhome']

# For better visualization, group households with 3 or more children
df['Children_Category'] = df['Children'].apply(lambda x: '3+' if x >= 3 else str(x))

# Remove extreme outliers for a clearer plot (top 1% of income and spending)
income_cap = df['Income'].quantile(0.99)
spending_cap = df['Total_Spending'].quantile(0.99)
df_plot = df[(df['Income'] < income_cap) & (df['Total_Spending'] < spending_cap)].copy()

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the style and create the figure and axes
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create the scatter plot to show the relationship between Income and Spending
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_plot,
    x='Income',
    y='Total_Spending',
    hue='Children_Category',
    hue_order=['0', '1', '2', '3+'], # Ensure logical order in legend
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.7,
    s=60,
    edgecolor='w',
    linewidth=0.5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Formatting and Labeling for Clarity ---
# Set a clear and descriptive title and subtitle
fig.suptitle(
    'The Impact of Income and Household Size on Customer Spending',
    fontsize=18,
    fontweight='bold',
    y=0.98
)
ax.set_title(
    'Customers with higher incomes tend to spend more, but this relationship is moderated by the number of children.',
    fontsize=12,
    pad=15
)

# Set axis labels
ax.set_xlabel('Annual Household Income', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Total Spending (Last 2 Years)', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)

# Format axis ticks with dollar signs and commas for readability
formatter = mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'${x:,.0f}')
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)
plt.xticks(rotation=30, ha='right')

# Customize the legend for better context
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax.legend(
    handles=handles,
    labels=labels,
    title='Number of Children',
    title_fontsize='11',
    fontsize='10',
    frameon=True,
    shadow=True,
    loc='upper left'
)

# Add a grid for easier value reading
ax.grid(True, which='both', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5)

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.95]) # Adjust rect to make space for suptitle

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
